RCT design: Open‐label prospective pilot, three parallel RCT (n = 31)
Primary outcome(s): Cumulative ulcer healing incidence after 12 weeks: Proportion healed: nAg 81.8%, MH 50%, conventional 40%. Ulcer size reduction rate: The nAg group had the highest reduction rate (97.45%), compared to the MH (86.24%) and conventional (76.91%) groups.

Trend toward better outcomes with Manuka: less skin distortion (1.6 vs. 1.8, p = 0.07), less palpable scar (1.8 vs. 2.0, p = 0.08), less stiffness (1.3 vs. 1.6, p = 0.058). No difference in grading at 1 or 4 months, but scar pain was significantly lower at 4 months (0.48 vs. 1.9, p = 0.005).
MHID vs. CD: faster healing (31 ± 4 vs. 43 ± 3 days, p < 0.05); higher sterilisation at week 1 (78.1% vs. 35.5%), but % ulcers healed similarly (97% vs. 90%).

The honey group showed faster infection clearance and shorter hospital stays (p < 0.05); higher complete healing rates at 6 weeks and 6 months (p < 0.05); fewer toe amputations (9.7% vs. 34.6%, p < 0.05); and no major amputations or deaths in either group.
MRSA eradicated in 70% of MH‐treated wounds vs. 16% with hydrogel after 4 weeks. P. aeruginosa cleared in 33% (MH) vs. 50% (hydrogel).

Comparator: Usual care (alginate, hydrofibre, hydrocolloid, foam, hydrogel, non‐adherent, iodine or silver dressings)
Primary outcome(s): Proportion of participants with a completely healed reference ulcer at 12 weeks: 55.6% (honey) vs. 49.7% (usual care); absolute increase 5.9% (95% CI −4.3 to 15.7), p = 0.258; no significant difference after adjustments.
